rv.q: It is a subtle and elegantly constructed piece of work.
The impact is muted, but the overall effect is disquieting.
The round shows Mary from all sides, in theory, yet you do not see her clearly at all.
Claire Allfree was disappointed that Susan Sarandon is only onstage for approximately 20 minutes: ‘audiences would be forgiven for expecting a bit more bang for their buck.
Letts wants to let us join the dots for ourselves, but the end result can feel more like a writing exercise than a fully satisfying play.
It’s a smart piece of writing that’s given us some fine performances - particularly from Riseborough - but its fussy theatricality ultimately gets in the way.
In their hands, this odd conceit just about works, creating images of a life both lived and wasted, pre-ordained and chosen.
